questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Shortest Distance Between a Point and a Plane Given in Simplified Dot Product Form
questions.problem: Given that $Q(0,5,2)$ lies on the plane $Π:r\cdot ⟨-6,2,3⟩=16$, find the shortest distance from $P(1,-4,5)$ to $Π.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we find

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{PQ} & =⟨0,5,2⟩-⟨1,-4,5⟩ \\  & =⟨-1,9,-3⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

From the equation of the plane, we get the normal vector $n=⟨-6,2,3⟩.$ 

Finally, the shortest distance from the point $P$ to the plane $Π$ is the absolute value of the scalar projection of $\overset{\to }{PQ}$ onto the normal vector of the plane:

$$
\begin{aligned}d & =|{\text{comp}}_{n}\,\overset{\to }{PQ}| \\  & =\frac{|\overset{\to }{PQ}\cdot n|}{|n|} \\  & =\frac{|(-1)\cdot (-6)+9\cdot 2+(-3)\cdot 3|}{\sqrt{(-6)^{2}+{2}^{2}+{3}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{|6+18-9|}{\sqrt{36+4+9}} \\  & =\frac{|15|}{\sqrt{49}} \\  & =\frac{15}{7}\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Given that $Q(1,3,5)$ lies on the plane $Π:r\cdot ⟨-4,1,-3⟩=-16$, find the shortest distance from $P(-3,7,3)$ to $Π.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we find

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{PQ} & =⟨1,3,5⟩-⟨-3,7,3⟩ \\  & =⟨4,-4,2⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

From the equation of the plane, we get the normal vector $n=⟨-4,1,-3⟩.$ 

Finally, the shortest distance from the point $P$ to the plane $Π$ is the absolute value of the scalar projection of $\overset{\to }{PQ}$ onto the normal vector of the plane:

$$
\begin{aligned}d & =|{\text{comp}}_{n}\,\overset{\to }{PQ}| \\  & =\frac{|\overset{\to }{PQ}\cdot n|}{|n|} \\  & =\frac{|4\cdot (-4)+(-4)\cdot 1+2\cdot (-3)|}{\sqrt{(-4)^{2}+{1}^{2}+(-3)^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{|-16-4-6|}{\sqrt{16+1+9}} \\  & =\frac{|-26|}{\sqrt{26}} \\  & =\sqrt{26}\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Find the shortest distance between the point $P(-3,-4,-8)$ and the plane $Π$ with equation $r\cdot ⟨-2,4,1⟩=3.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we need to find a point on the plane. If $r=⟨x,y,z⟩,$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨x,y,z⟩\cdot ⟨-2,4,1⟩ & =3 \\ -2x+4y+z & =3 \\ z & =3+2x-4y.\end{aligned}
$$

Setting $x=1$ and $y=1,$ we get 

$$
z=3+2(1)-4(1)=1.
$$

So, the point $Q(1,1,1)$ lies on the plane. 

Now, we find

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{PQ} & =⟨1,1,1⟩-⟨-3,-4,-8⟩ \\  & =⟨4,5,9⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

From the equation of a plane, we get a normal vector $n=⟨-2,4,1⟩.$

Finally, the shortest distance from the point $P$ to the plane $Π$ is the absolute value of the scalar projection of $\overset{\to }{PQ}$ onto the normal vector of the plane:

$$
\begin{aligned}d & =|{\text{comp}}_{n}\,\overset{\to }{PQ}| \\  & =\frac{|\overset{\to }{PQ}\cdot n|}{|n|} \\  & =\frac{|4\cdot (-2)+5\cdot 4+9\cdot 1|}{\sqrt{(-2)^{2}+{4}^{2}+{1}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{|-8+20+9|}{\sqrt{4+16+1}} \\  & =\frac{|21|}{\sqrt{21}} \\  & =\sqrt{21}\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Shortest Distance Between a Point and a Plane Given in Cartesian Form
questions.problem: Find the shortest distance between the point $P(5,4,-4)$ and the plane $Π$ with equation $6x-3y+6z=-18.$
questions.worked_solution:
Let's start by picking a point on the plane. To do that, we simply substitute some concrete values for $x$ and $y$ into the equation and solve for $z.$ Let's choose $x=1$ and $y=2$ (though it doesn't really matter what values we choose). Solving for $z,$ we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}6x-3y+6z & =-18 \\ 6(1)-3(2)+6z & =-18 \\ 6z & =-18 \\ z & =-3.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we get the point $Q(1,2,-3)$ which lies on the plane.

Computing $\overset{\to }{PQ},$ we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{PQ} & =⟨1,2,-3⟩-⟨5,4,-4⟩ \\  & =⟨-4,-2,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

We also need a normal vector to the plane. For any Cartesian equation of a plane $ax+by+cz=d,$ the normal vector is $n=⟨a,b,c⟩.$ So, for the plane $Π,$ we have $n=⟨6,-3,6⟩.$ 

Finally, the shortest distance from the point $P$ to the plane $Π$ is the absolute value of the scalar projection of $\overset{\to }{PQ}$ onto the normal vector of the plane:

$$
\begin{aligned}d & =|{\text{comp}}_{n}\,\overset{\to }{PQ}| \\  & =\frac{|\overset{\to }{PQ}\cdot n|}{|n|} \\  & =\frac{|(-4)\cdot 6+(-2)\cdot (-3)+1\cdot 6|}{\sqrt{{6}^{2}+(-3)^{2}+{6}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{|-24+6+6|}{\sqrt{36+9+36}} \\  & =\frac{|\,-12\,|}{\sqrt{81}} \\  & =\frac{4}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Find the shortest distance between the point $P(-2,3,-6)$ and the plane $Π$ with equation $-x+2y+2z=8.$
questions.worked_solution:
Let's start by picking a point on the plane. To do that, we simply substitute some concrete values for $x$ and $y$ into the equation and solve for $z.$ Let's choose $x=-2$ and $y=1$ (though it doesn't really matter what values we choose). Solving for $z,$ we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}-x+2y+2z & =8 \\ -1(-2)+2(1)+2z & =8 \\ 2z & =4 \\ z & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we get the point $Q(-2,1,2)$ which lies on the plane.

Computing $\overset{\to }{PQ},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{PQ} & =⟨-2,1,2⟩-⟨-2,3,-6⟩ \\  & =⟨0,-2,8⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

We also need a normal vector to the plane. For any Cartesian equation of a plane $ax+by+cz=d,$ the normal vector is $n=⟨a,b,c⟩.$ So, for the plane $Π,$ we have $n=⟨-1,2,2⟩.$ 

Finally, the shortest distance from the point $P$ to the plane $Π$ is the absolute value of the scalar projection of $\overset{\to }{PQ}$ onto the normal vector of the plane:

$$
\begin{aligned}d & =|{\text{comp}}_{n}\,\overset{\to }{PQ}| \\  & =\frac{|\overset{\to }{PQ}\cdot n|}{|n|} \\  & =\frac{|0\cdot (-1)+(-2)\cdot 2+8\cdot 2|}{\sqrt{(-1)^{2}+{2}^{2}+{2}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{|0-4+16|}{\sqrt{1+4+4}} \\  & =\frac{|12|}{\sqrt{9}} \\  & =\frac{12}{3} \\  & =4.\end{aligned}
$$
